title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations
abstract: arXiv:2611.18089v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The hidden layers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are believed to encode representations of the data whose abstraction increases with depth. However, in the absence of an operational notion of abstraction, this statement is hard to test quantitatively. Here, we propose an alternative view, building on the principle that the correlations of a sequence reflect the structure of the process that generated it. We define the autocorrelation function of a layer as the average dot product between its activations at two context positions separated by a lag. Latent variables encoded persistently along the context create slowly decaying tails in the autocorrelation, and we find these tails to grow across layers in both synthetic and natural data. In synthetic data with controlled hierarchical latent structure, this growth stems from the encoding of abstract latent variables, which govern long stretches of the input. translated_title: 深层潜变量，长记忆：潜变量持久性解释Transformer激活中的时间相关性
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）的隐藏层被认为编码了数据表示，其抽象程度随深度增加。然而，由于缺乏可操作的抽象概念定义，这一说法难以进行定量检验。在此，我们提出了另一种视角，其基础原理是：序列的相关性反映了生成该序列的过程的结构。我们将某一层的自相关函数定义为其在两个相隔一定滞后的上下文位置上的激活之间的平均点积。沿上下文持续编码的潜变量会在自相关中产生缓慢衰减的尾部，我们发现在合成数据和自然数据中，这些尾部都会随层加深而增长。在具有受控层级潜变量结构的合成数据中，这种增长源于对抽象潜变量的编码，这些潜变量支配着输入的长片段。事实上，潜变量的持久性……
tldr: 该论文提出用层激活的自相关函数作为抽象的可操作度量，发现潜变量的持久编码会在自相关中产生慢衰减尾部，且这些尾部随Transformer层加深而增长，从而解释了深层模型编码抽象潜变量的机制。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the autocorrelation function of layer activations as an operational measure of abstraction, showing that slowly decaying tails from persistent latent encoding grow across transformer layers, explaining how depth encodes abstract latent variables.
